title: Expected randomized value of a signed clause
statement: Let $\sigma:\{1,2,3\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and let $\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3\in[-1,1]$. For each sign $b\in\{−1,1\}$, form the three signs obtained from $(1,b,b)$ by negating coordinate $i$ exactly when $\sigma_i$ is true, and consider the three-literal clause that rejects precisely this sign triple. The uniform average over $b$ of the clause's randomized value at coordinate means $\mu$ equals $1/2$ plus one half the randomized value at $\mu$ of the OXR predicate with its inputs negated according to $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ assigns a Boolean value to each of three coordinates
caveat: The supplied formal snippet does not include the definition of the OXR predicate, so its randomized-value term on the right cannot be fully unpacked into a self-contained description.
